label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (a1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, when the observed inputs show this trial chose a1 (in_action=1) and reached S2 (in_state=2), i.e. a rare transition after a1. It never fires at D1, almost never at GO (66 steps), and not on a2->S2, a2->S1 or a1->S1. Dev F1 0.945, precision 0.90, recall 0.998. Magnitude is weaker when the previous trial was also a rare transition: excluding those cases drops recall in the lowest activation quartile to 0.38 while the top quartiles are kept, so the activation is largest for a1->S2 transitions that are isolated / unexpected. The rare a1->S2 transition is observed at D2, so no future variable is used.

issues: The core claims hold. Phase profile (dev): D1 0 active, GO 66, D2 41035, with 100% of activation mass at D2. Test scores for the original predicate reproduce: P 0.891, R 0.997, F1 0.941. Misses: 119 test steps, mostly weak GO activations holding 0.0% of the mass, so they are noise.

The false positives (5098 on test) are not noise. They come mostly from a repeated a1->S2 transition. When the previous trial was also a1->S2, precision falls to 0.63 (8735 steps). When the previous trial was a1->S2 AND rewarded (prev_reward==1), the unit is silent on all 1477 such steps (precision 0.000). When the two previous trials were both a1->S2, precision is 0.28.

The explanation says the unit is weaker when the previous trial was 'also rare'. That is wrong about the cause. If the previous trial was a rare transition in the other direction (a2->S1), precision is 0.98 (1044 steps). The suppression is specific to a previous a1->S2 transition, strongest when it was rewarded. prev_common==0 only looks predictive because it mostly overlaps with a previous a1->S2.

Good state matters a little, which goes against the claim that it adds nothing. Precision is 0.83 when good==S2 and 0.91 when good==S1, so the unit is somewhat weaker when S2 is good, i.e. when landing in S2 is less surprising for value.

A better observed-only predicate removes the systematic silent class. It excludes trials where the previous trial was a rewarded a1->S2: test P 0.923, R 0.997, F1 0.959. Also excluding two consecutive prior a1->S2 trials gives test F1 0.962 (P 0.938, R 0.988). The remaining false positives still look like a recency effect: a1->S2 one or two trials back.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 after an a1->S2 (rare) transition, suppressed when the previous trial was also an a1->S2 transition (silent if that one was rewarded)
